Some pieces of advice (I actually have so many HAHA but here's a few):

1. Be humble! especially on your first job. I started working by doing menial stuff for marketing and sales. Carried and counted inventory. Went to clients and physically demo-ed products. Arranged displays for marketing. Stood in front of crowds calling for customers. You will earn more respect from others if you do those things. I still do those things now!

2. Learn how to adapt to different people. Learn how to read their expressions and intentions. Learn how to adapt to wherever you're placed in. Learn how to do politics if necessary. These are things that take effort but will really be good for you in the long run.

3. On joining startups - remember: startups that burn money really easily (unnecessary parties, extra bonuses, unusually high salaries) but don't actually make any profits will likely fail sooner than you expect.

4. Nobody does presentations in real life the way they teach you in school. Nobody actually likes presentations, haha. It's how you communicate your message that's the most important. More than making your slides pretty, put 99% of the effort into making your message work for your audience.

5. EXCEL IS LIFE. MASTER IT NOW. Almost everything requires some form of analytics now. You can start with getting sales data and manipulating it by thinking of results-oriented questions like "How did my product category XX do in 2017? Is it enough to reach YY growth in 2018?" Something like that. Everyone will praise you for good data manipulation and interpretation skills. (DON'T GET USED TO VLOOKUP, USE INDEX(MATCH)!! IT'S MUCH SEXIER HAHA)
